hypothesis: If fishes approach a maximal size only asymptotically, then mean length at age in well-sampled wild fish populations keeps increasing, by ever smaller but still positive increments, through the oldest well-sampled ages, and an asymptotic growth model fits the length-at-age means better than a model in which length reaches a fixed maximum at a finite age and then stays there.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: ICES DATRAS North Sea IBTS (NS-IBTS) age records (CA record type), quarters 1 and 3, survey years 2000-2024, all species; length class converted to cm; records with a plus-group flag or missing age excluded. A species qualifies if it has at least 7 consecutive age classes starting at age 1, each with at least 50 aged fish (sum of CANoAtLngt); the included age range ends at the oldest class with at least 50 fish. For each species, mean length at age is computed (weighted by CANoAtLngt) and two 3-parameter models are fitted by weighted least squares (weights = number of fish): (i) asymptotic von Bertalanffy L = Linf (1 - exp(-K (a - t0))) with K > 0, and (ii) determinate quadratic-plateau L = Lmax - c (tc - a)^2 for a < tc, L = Lmax for a >= tc, with tc constrained to at most (oldest included age - 1) so that the model asserts a maximum actually reached inside the data. dAIC = AIC_det - AIC_VB (positive favours the asymptotic model). Late-age increments are the three increments of mean length between the last four included age classes. SUPPORTS if the asymptotic model is favoured (dAIC > 2) in at least two thirds of qualifying species AND at least 75% of all late-age increments pooled across species are positive. Requires at least 5 qualifying species; otherwise inconclusive (underpowered).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the determinate model is favoured (dAIC < -2) in at least half of the qualifying species, OR if at least half of the pooled late-age increments are zero or negative (growth has stopped at a reached maximum while fish are still well sampled). Anything between the supports and refutes conditions is 'mixed'. If the DATRAS download API is unreachable the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
interpretation: Thompson's 'size never actually reaches, but only approaches asymptotically, a maximal limit' is read as a contrast between an asymptotic growth curve (increments decline toward zero but stay positive at every age reached) and determinate growth (a maximum reached at a finite age, with zero increments thereafter while the animals are alive). 'Size' is taken as body length, the quantity recorded in surveys. The test uses cross-sectional survey means of length at age rather than individual growth histories; this is a modern reinterpretation forced by the data (Thompson's own fish examples were also population means). Fitted asymptotic parameters are not themselves used as evidence of an asymptote, as one assessor warned; the evidence is the model comparison against an explicit reached-maximum alternative and the sign of the late-age increments.
